narrative_purpose: Grounds the cyclone section in what canon actually shows - a genuinely oceanic sea with deep swell and organised squall lines - so the heat-engine argument arrives attached to weather the reader has seen.
subject: An open seascape under a gas giant sky. Long dark ocean swell runs in from the far distance, its crests torn into spray by strong wind. Across the middle distance a low squall line stretches the full width of the frame as a continuous dark shelf of cloud, with sheets of rain trailing from its underside down onto the water. Faint bioluminescence glows in the breaking wave tops. No land and no vessel anywhere in the frame.
scene: Open ocean far from any coast during a passing squall, the banded limb of the gas giant dim behind the cloud.
camera: Low viewpoint just above the water surface, looking out across the swell toward the squall line, horizon low so the cloud shelf dominates.
light: Overcast and directionless, dimmed by the squall; a narrow band of brighter sky at the horizon beneath the cloud shelf, and cool bioluminescent glow in the foam.
palette: Deep ocean-teal water, near-black storm cloud, cool grey-teal rain sheets, faint misty-cyan bioluminescence in the crests, dim amber-grey gas-giant limb.
style: Painterly naturalist seascape, hand-painted water and cloud with real weight, NOT a photograph and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: High on the wave crests and torn spray in the foreground; the squall line's rain shafts distinct but soft; far distance dissolving into rain haze.
composition: Strong horizontal banding - foreground swell, mid-distance rain shafts, dark cloud shelf above - with the brighter horizon gap and open water areas left plain for callouts.
consistency_notes: Ocean in the same deep ocean-teal used for Pandoran seas elsewhere in the book; rain and spray in the chapter's water-in-air cyan. Keep the frame empty of craft, creatures and coastline so the weather is the whole subject.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no boats, no vessels, no land, no creatures, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look
